result.title: Protein Functional Semantic Alignment via Representation Rectification
result.summary: Protein language models (PLMs) are commonly pretrained with likelihood-based objectives such as masked language modeling or denoising. These objectives capture sequence-level regularities, but can produce representations in which functional signals are entangled with non-functional variation (e.g., sequence identity, compositional bias, and frequent local motifs), creating a readout bottleneck for downstream function prediction. We introduce Functional Semantic Alignment via Representation Rectification (SAVR), a contrastive post-training method using Pfam family co-membership as a homology-guided discrete semantic signal to reshape PLM representations. SAVR reduces directional dominance and redistributes variance across embedding dimensions, decreasing variance concentration, and increasing effective dimensionality of the embedding covariance spectrum. Without observing any task-specific labels during post-training, SAVR achieves state-of-the-art results on Enzyme Commission (EC) benchmarks and competitive results on Gene Ontology (GO) benchmarks under frozen-backbone evaluation. These results suggest that homology-guided contrastive post-training can rectify PLM representation geometry and improve sequence-based protein function prediction.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SAVR，以 Pfam 家族共成员作为同源引导的离散语义信号进行对比后训练，矫正蛋白质语言模型的表示几何：降低方向主导、重分配方差并提升嵌入协方差谱的有效维度，在冻结骨干下改进 EC/GO 功能预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用离散语义信号做对比后训练以矫正表示几何、提升有效维度」的做法，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理状态的维度坍缩与信息集中问题提供可供核查的训练侧线索，但同视觉推理无直接关联。
